title: The Halvek Constitution (1934)
content:
## The Constitution of 1934

The current governing document of the Republic — technically an amendment of the 1897 Constitution, functionally a replacement. Drafted by Halvek's legal committee in the months following the coup.

## Key Articles

**Article 22 — Executive Powers:** Grants the Chancellor the authority to dissolve parliament, appoint judges, issue executive orders with the force of law, and declare states of emergency without legislative approval. This is the article that makes the Chancellorship an autocracy in legal form.

**Article 31 — Amendment Procedure:** Requires a two-thirds parliamentary supermajority for any constitutional change. This means the Halvekist minority can block reform indefinitely.

**Article 45 — Judicial Appointments:** All judges appointed by the Chancellor serve for life. Every judge currently sitting was appointed by Halvek or his ministers.

## The Reform Project

The constitutional reform movement seeks to abolish Articles 22, reform Articles 31 and 45, and restore the democratic provisions of the 1897 Constitution. The central dilemma: using Article 22 to abolish Article 22 means using Halvek's tools to dismantle Halvek's system. Whether this is legitimate or hypocritical is the central constitutional debate of the Ashavel government.

title: Executive Orders
content:
## Executive Orders Under Article 22

Article 22 grants the Chancellor the power to issue executive orders with the full force of law. These orders do not require parliamentary approval and cannot be challenged in ordinary courts — only the Constitutional Court can review them, and the Constitutional Court's judges were all appointed by Halvek.

## Historical Usage

Halvek issued approximately 800 executive orders over twenty-six years — governing by decree while maintaining the fiction of parliamentary democracy. The transitional government issued 47, mostly procedural. Katerin Ashavel's government has issued a handful — each one scrutinized as evidence of authoritarian tendencies.

## Political Calculus

Executive orders allow the Chancellor to govern effectively when parliament is gridlocked. They also confirm the Halvekist narrative that the new government is no different from the old one. Every executive order is simultaneously an act of governance and an act of self-indictment.

title: The Constitutional Reform Process
content:
## Paths to Constitutional Reform

There are two paths to replacing the Halvek Constitution:

### The Legislative Path
Build a two-thirds parliamentary coalition for reform by persuading moderate Halvekists to support specific constitutional changes. Advantages: legitimate, durable, difficult to reverse. Disadvantages: slow, uncertain, requires cooperation from the very faction the reforms are designed to disempower.

### The Executive Path
Use Article 22 to call a constitutional convention by executive order, bypassing the parliamentary supermajority requirement. Advantages: fast, legally effective. Disadvantages: uses Halvek's own power-grab mechanism, undermining the democratic legitimacy of whatever constitution emerges.

Both paths are being actively debated within the government. Neither has a clear majority.
